claim_tested: SelO-fold proteins are AMPylases and the fold has a defined nucleotide/Mg2+ active site
key_finding: SelO transfers AMP from ATP to Ser/Thr/Tyr; crystal structure of a SelO homolog shows a protein-kinase-like fold with ATP flipped in the active site; SelO pseudokinases localize to mitochondria and AMPylate redox proteins
context: Pseudomonas syringae SelO (PDB 6EAC), E. coli, human and yeast homologs; in vitro AMPylation and cell assays
confidence_and_limitations: High for the family. Does not test S. pombe sel0.

claim_tested: A fungal SelO ortholog is a catalytically active AMPylase in vivo and in vitro
key_finding: Fmp40 AMPylates Prx1, Trx3 and Grx2 in vitro and interacts with Trx3 in vivo; FMP40 deletion alters the H2O2 response, PCD induction and GSH/NADPH pools; Thr66 of Trx3 is the AMPylation site
confidence_and_limitations: High. Closest experimentally validated fungal relative (38.2% id to PsSelO); still a different species from S. pombe.

claim_tested: Metazoan SELENOO AMPylates mitochondrial metabolic enzymes
key_finding: Mammalian Selenoprotein O regulates metabolic flux by AMPylating mitochondrial proteins including glutamate dehydrogenase and pyruvate dehydrogenase, identified with a hinT-based enrichment platform
confidence_and_limitations: High for mammals. Substrate set is organism-specific and should not be transferred to S. pombe.

claim_tested: The SelO reference active site can be defined objectively from ligand contacts
key_finding: 23 protein-ligand contacts in chain A: 21 residues within 4.0 A of AMP-PNP; only N253 (OD1, 2.12 A) and D262 (OD2, 2.23 A) within 3.2 A of Mg2+; K113 NZ contacts O2G (2.74 A) and O2B (2.98 A) and salt-bridges E136 OE1 (2.67 A)
confidence_and_limitations: High. Single chain analysed; hydrogens are modelled, so the shortest contacts involve H atoms.

claim_tested: sel0 retains the ATP-binding Lys and Glu the catalytic Asp and the Mg2+-binding residues
key_finding: BLOSUM62 global alignment of sel0 to PsSelO (36.6% id over 476 columns) maps all 10 reference positions: D91>D121, R93>R123, K113>K144, D125>D156, E136>E167, R176>R208, R183>R215, D252>D287, N253>N288, D262>D297, all identical
context: S. pombe O13890 vs PsSelO Q87VB1
confidence_and_limitations: High for core motif positions (unambiguous motif context: LGDGR, QVKGAGR, LRSSIRE, NTDNTS, DYGPF); lower for peripheral loop arginines where gap placement varies between alignment runs.

claim_tested: The conserved residues form an assembled active site rather than scattered positions
key_finding: AlphaFold v6 model (mean pLDDT 95.75; catalytic residues pLDDT 87.6-98.5) reproduces PsSelO active-site distances: Pearson r = 0.952, median offset 0.36 A; K144-E167 salt bridge 3.85 A (apo) vs 2.67 A in nucleotide-bound 6EAC
context: Predicted structure of S. pombe sel0
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate-high. The model is apo and unliganded; no nucleotide or metal was docked. AlphaFold is partly trained on homologs, so this is not fully independent of the alignment.

claim_tested: Residue conservation in sel0 discriminates sel0 from other fungal SelO proteins
key_finding: Across 70 fungal PF02696 proteins (one per genus, 400-1000 aa) the reference positions are conserved at 92.9-100%; 91.4% retain all 10. sel0 is at the family baseline, not an outlier.
confidence_and_limitations: High. The panel is one sequence per genus from UniProt and is biased toward well-sequenced Ascomycota; it shows the test has little discriminating power within fungi.

claim_tested: Existing site annotations agree with the independently derived positions
key_finding: UniProt annotates Active site 287 (proton acceptor) and Binding sites 120, 122, 123, 144, 156, 157, 208, 215, 288, 297, all ECO:0000250; this analysis derived 287, 144, 156, 208, 215, 288, 297 independently and differs by one position in the Gly-rich loop
context: Database record; protein existence level 3 (inferred from homology)
confidence_and_limitations: Database-level support only. ECO:0000250 means these sites are themselves homology transfers, so the agreement is methodological corroboration, not independent evidence.

claim_tested: There is experimental evidence for sel0 function in S. pombe
key_finding: All 11 GO annotations are non-experimental: GO:0070733 (ISS from Q08968, IBA, IEA from RHEA:54288, 4x ISO), GO:0005739 (IBA, ISS, IEA), GO:0098869 (IC from GO:0070733). No primary S. pombe paper on sel0 was found in PubMed.
confidence_and_limitations: High confidence that no experimental evidence exists as of this search. Absence of a PubMed hit does not exclude unindexed high-throughput datasets.

citation: PMID:9700395 (cited by a PomBase ISO annotation)
claim_tested: The ISO reference supporting GO:0070733 for sel0 is appropriate
key_finding: PMID:9700395 resolves to 'Education and research: where are we going?' (Australian Veterinary Journal, 1998), which does not concern AMPylation
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. May be a QuickGO mapping artefact rather than a PomBase error; a curator should check the underlying annotation file.

claim_tested: The ten-position mapping is an artefact of one alignment parameter choice
key_finding: Across 10 gap-penalty settings (open -5 to -20, extend -0.5 to -2.0) sel0 identity to PsSelO ranged 35.5-40.7%, yet all ten reference positions mapped to the identical sel0 residue in every run (D121, R123, K144, D156, E167, R208, R215, D287, N288, D297); 1 distinct assignment per position for all four comparator proteins
context: sel0, Fmp40, YdiU, human SELENOO aligned to PsSelO Q87VB1
confidence_and_limitations: High for the scored positions. Still pairwise alignment, not a profile HMM or structure-based alignment; positions outside the scored set (e.g. PsSelO R165) do move and were excluded.

claim_tested: A 10/10 catalytic-residue score is informative rather than automatic
key_finding: Of 254 PF02696 proteins (one per genus, 380-1000 aa) across Bacteria, Archaea, Fungi, Metazoa, Viridiplantae and other eukaryotes, 16 (6.3%) lose at least one of the five core catalytic residues (K113, E136, D252, N253, D262 by PsSelO numbering); 11/244 (4.5%) among entries above 35% identity and 5/10 below it. Bacteria and Archaea are 100% conserved at all ten positions. Arg93 is 100% in prokaryotes but 11.7% in Metazoa. sel0 scores 10/10 and core5 5/5.
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate-high. One sequence per genus from UniProt, biased toward well-sequenced clades; low-identity failures are likely fragmentary gene models rather than true pseudoenzymes, so 6.3% is an upper bound on real catalytic loss.

claim_tested: sel0's extra 81 residues over PsSelO perturb the catalytic core
key_finding: sel0 is 568 aa vs 487 for PsSelO with 88 inserted residues in six blocks of 3 aa or more: a 30-aa N-terminal extension, then 28 aa after PsSelO 313, 10 aa after 384, 9 aa after 373, 8 aa after 477 and 3 aa after 212. Nearest insertion to any catalytic position is 29 residues away. sel0 has 18 Cys and no selenocysteine.
context: Pairwise alignment geometry of O13890 vs Q87VB1
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. Insertion boundaries depend on the alignment; block sizes are approximate. Says the core is colinear, not that the insertions are functionless.

claim_tested: Experimental interaction data exist for sel0 that could identify substrates
key_finding: SPAC20G4.05c resolves to 284812.O13890 (STRING preferredName fmp40). All 10 returned partners (ppk26 0.792, mxr2 0.594, SPCC61.04c 0.570, SPAC1F7.11c 0.519, bcp1 0.503, ept1 0.476, mxr1 0.454, cyc2 0.425, csn2 0.405, cut6 0.404) have an experimental subscore of 0.0. Highest non-textmining channel is a gene-fusion score of 0.464 to bcp1, a peroxiredoxin-family gene.
confidence_and_limitations: Database-level only. Absence in STRING does not prove no experiment exists, but it is consistent with the PubMed and QuickGO results. The bcp1 fusion score is a computed channel and echoes the Fmp40-Prx1 link (PMID:38795545) without measuring it.

claim_tested: The ISS transfer of GO:0070733 from Q08968 to O13890 could be paralog confusion rather than orthology
key_finding: S. pombe, S. cerevisiae and E. coli each contain exactly one PF02696 protein (O13890 568 aa, Q08968 688 aa, P77649 478 aa); human contains two (Q9BVL4 and unreviewed Q6ICA4). Smith-Waterman reciprocal best-hit test over full reviewed proteomes: O13890 vs 6733 S. cerevisiae proteins gives Q08968 at SW 826 with runner-up 58; Q08968 vs 5129 S. pombe proteins gives O13890 at SW 839 with runner-up 63. Reciprocal in both directions, 14-fold margin.
context: Full reviewed proteomes of S. pombe 284812 and S. cerevisiae 559292
confidence_and_limitations: High. Restricted to UniProt reviewed entries, so an unreviewed paralog is not formally excluded, though no PF02696 unreviewed entry was returned for either yeast. Orthology licenses the transfer; it does not make the evidence experimental.

claim_tested: Sequence features give independent support for the mitochondrial CC annotation GO:0005739 on sel0
key_finding: Net charge of the first 40 residues separates 275 S. pombe transit-peptide proteins from 65 cytosolic ones at AUC 0.930 (mean +5.14 vs -0.60, Cohen's d = 1.99); Arg count AUC 0.802. sel0 scores +2 with 1 Arg and 4 acidic residues, the 5.5th percentile of transit peptides. The positive control fails the same way: Fmp40, experimentally mitochondrial, is at the 6.4th percentile and human SELENOO at the 10.2nd. Stable across windows of 20-60 residues (background AUC 0.916-0.953).
context: UniProt reference sets for S. pombe and S. cerevisiae; five SelO-family comparators
confidence_and_limitations: Null result, reported as such. The feature has no sensitivity in this family, so it is evidence neither for nor against mitochondrial localization of sel0. Composition-only test; no trained predictor (TargetP, MitoFates) was run, and those could still differ.
